meta.margin_convention: margin = Democratic (or independent) minus Republican, percentage points; positive favors D/I
meta.p_dem: probability for the D (or listed I) candidate in races_to_check.json
meta.verified: true = read from forecaster's own data/page; false = secondary report or rating-only
meta.wayback_note: web.archive.org blocked scripted requests (429/'abusive bot traffic') during this research; most numbers come from forecasters' own live data files that still carry the final Nov 2-3 run, checked by timestamp.

ddhq.name: Decision Desk HQ / The Hill
ddhq.notes: Probabilistic model covering Senate, House, Governor (36 races). DDHQ site (and its Wayback captures) return HTTP 429 Vercel bot checkpoint to curl/WebFetch, so no primary page was read. All numbers secondary: Newsweek (Nov 3), Cillizza/DDHQ podcast post (Nov 2, 'second-to-last run'), Vote-Scope comparison, FiftyPlusOne post-mortem (Nov 5), search-engine summaries of DDHQ pages, 270toWin category map (Nov 2). Race-level probabilities found for only 8 Senate and 7 governor races; others have rating band only.

fiftyplusone.name: FiftyPlusOne (G. Elliott Morris)
fiftyplusone.notes: Senate + House model only; no governor forecast (site routes are /forecast, /forecast/house, /forecast/senate; /forecast/governor 404). Full race-level data read from the live SvelteKit __data.json, which on 2026-11-11 still carries model_date 2026-11-03 / timestamp 2026-11-03T05:53:08Z (final pre-election run, not post-election data). FPO is G. Elliott Morris's outfit; Strength In Numbers is his Substack (handled elsewhere). Raw: dl_ddhq/fpo_senate_all_dec.json, fpo_house_all_dec.json.

votehub.name: VoteHub
votehub.notes: Published a probabilistic 2026 midterm model (launched May 4, 2026; House + Senate; governor coverage not confirmed). votehub.com is behind a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); no race-level numbers obtained. Chamber numbers are secondary.

economist.name: The Economist
economist.notes: Senate+House model only (25,001 sims, polls from FiftyPlusOne). No governor model: site nav lists only Senate/House, no governor page in Wayback, CDN governor paths return 403, and Wikipedia's governor ratings table has no Economist column. Final run timestamp 2026-11-03 07:20 UTC (pre-polls; days_before_vote=0). Wayback snapshot of 2026-11-04 01:06 UTC shows Nov 3 'Latest news' text: Dems 52% for Senate ('our model is now a substantial outlier'), House 93% with average 234 D seats; snapshot's interactive data did not archive, so per-race numbers were taken from the Economist's live CDN data files, which still carry date 2026-11-03 and match the archived prose (0.5166 Senate, 0.928 House). Senate seat counts in Economist files: dem_* includes independents caucusing with D (Osborn, Bengs, Achilles, Bodnar listed in independents.csv). Newsweek 2026-11-03 margins (NC +9, GA +7, NH +6, MN +4, ME/MI +3, OH <1; R: TX/KS <1, AK 1, IA 3, SC 4, NE 6, FL 8) are consistent with the data file. Data-file oddity: SC Republican listed as 'Darline Graham'.

polymarket.name: Polymarket
polymarket.notes: p_dem = last hourly price-history point (Yes token of the Dem/I outcome) at or before 2026-11-03T12:00Z (points stamped ~11:00Z). p_dem_pre_close = last point before 23:00Z (stamped ~22:00Z), before the first polls closed. Race markets are the 2026 "<state>-senate-election-winner" / "<state>-governor-winner-2026" events (not the older 2024-dated "-us-senate-election-winner" events). All race markets covered. Polymarket prices are not normalized; Dem+R can sum to slightly over/under 1.

kalshi.name: Kalshi
kalshi.notes: p_dem = last traded price (hourly candle price.close) at or before 2026-11-03T12:00Z; yes_bid/yes_ask are the closing quotes of the last candle in that window. Ticker quirks: Kentucky Senate is event SENATELA-26 (titled and ruled as Kentucky); Louisiana Senate is KXSENATELA-26NOV; Florida and Ohio Senate are SENATEFLS-26/SENATEOHS-26; Kansas Governor is GOVPARTYKS-27 (rules: Kansas 2026 election); NH Governor is GOVPARTYNH-28 (subtitle "In 2026", settled on the 2026 race); Alaska Governor uses party market KXGOVPARTYAK-26 (candidate market KXGOVAK-26 also recorded). All race markets covered.

sin.name: Strength In Numbers (G. Elliott Morris)
sin.notes: No separate SIN race-level model. Morris's 2026 forecast IS the FiftyPlusOne (50+1) model, which he builds; SIN's Aug 3 launch post is a crosspost of the 50+1 forecast, and the Nov 3 'FINAL forecast' post links 'my forecasting model' to fiftyplusone.news/forecast/senate and says it gives Democrats 'a roughly 8-in-10 chance of winning majorities in both chambers' (rest of post is registration-walled). Use FiftyPlusOne numbers (covered by another fork); do not double-count. Morris also has a fundamentals-only interactive at projects.gelliottmorris.com (no race-level probabilities).

cnalysis.name: CNalysis, now rebranded State Navigate
cnalysis.notes: cnalysis.com now serves State Navigate. 2026 coverage: state legislatures plus statewide offices (Governor, Lt. Gov., AG) with win probabilities and vote shares. No U.S. Senate or U.S. House forecast (forecast-sen/ussen pages 404; national page covers state legislative seats only). All 25 governor races in our list are covered. Pages are live but stamped 'Updated: November 3, 2026' (Alaska: Nov 2), so these are the final pre-election numbers. Margin = projected D share minus R share. Alaska is RCV: probability is 'wins X% of modeled scenarios', margin is on first-choice votes. Values shown as '<1%' or '>99%' are kept as text with p_dem null.

538.name: 538 (ABC News)
538.notes: Disney/ABC shut down 538 on March 5, 2025 and laid off about 15 staff. On May 15, 2026 ABC redirected all archived 538 content to abcnews.com/politics. There was no 2026 538 forecast. Source: Wikipedia, citing WSJ 2025-03-04 and NYT 2026-05-16.

jhk.name: JHK Forecasts (Jack Kersting)
jhk.notes: Page says 'Forecast frozen November 2, 2026'; JSON date 2026-11-02, 20,000 draws. Numbers are from the default 'Standard' (polls + fundamentals) version; 'Plus', 'Simple' and 'Now Cast' versions also exist (saved as jhk/senate-plus.json etc.; Plus gives Dem Senate control 0.795). Covers Senate and House; no governor forecast (/2026/governor/ returns 404). Margin = D (or I) vote share minus R share x100. Senate median derived from the published simulation histogram ('outcomes').

leantossup.name: LeanTossup.ca
leantossup.notes: Canadian forecaster (best known for Canadian elections) with a full 2026 US House/Senate/Governor model. Files say updated 2026-11-02T22:22:10Z, as_of 2026-11-02. Fields: pd = P(Dem, or the independent in ID/NE/SD), m = projected margin. Some data quirks: MN Senate/Gov Dem name blank, AK Senate GOP name blank, SC GOP listed as 'Darline Graham' (JHK and ElectIt have the same name, likely from a shared candidate file). In Montana LT models Bankhead (D), not Bodnar (I), so its MT number is for the Democrat.

electit.name: ElectIt (Ebanks, Katz & King, Harvard/Caltech)
electit.notes: Academic House and Senate model (LogisTiCC). Numbers are 'Our Forecast' = the 'Model + All Polls' version, from the precomputed snapshot taken 2026-11-03T03:15:46Z (RCP generic ballot D+8.8, 11/02). The page code says the frozen snapshots keep the figures as written before Nov 6. Also published: a Post-Nomination (no polls) version and a Model + Generic Ballot version. No governor forecast. ElectIt treats Bodnar (MT) as the 'D' side. Margin = card 'ap' (projected D-R margin).

pec.name: Princeton Election Consortium (Sam Wang)
pec.notes: Chamber-level snapshot only (Nov 3 post; graphic stamped 'Updated Nov 2, 2026'): Senate D+I control 84%, median 52, expected 52.5; House generic ballot D+8.4%, meta-lead D+5.4% (no House probability published). No race-level probabilities. Read from the post's image, saved as dl_misc/pec_snapshot.png.

others_not_recorded.name: Other models seen but not recorded
others_not_recorded.notes: Hobbyist or low-profile 2026 models found through web search; their numbers were not collected. Vote-Scope's comparison page is a secondary aggregator (dates Nov 1-4) that lists Silver 80.0%, FPO 79.0%, RTWH 77.5%, Split Ticket 77.0%, Economist 53%, VoteHub 67.9% for Dem Senate control (search-snippet level, unverified); it could cross-check the other forks. The Downballot, Elections Daily, Sabato, Cook and Inside Elections publish ratings only. The NYT returned 403 and the WaPo URL failed; no evidence either published a 2026 probabilistic model. On Point / VT Analytics is being handled by the parent.

onpoint.name: On Point Politics forecast (On Point Polling / VT Analytics)
onpoint.notes: Small, little-known pollster/forecaster; reputability not established. Frozen final bundle (manifest with SHA-256; model.json hash verified cc9fb4f5...). Its post-election accuracy page is self-promotional. Covers all Senate, House, governor races. Only forecast to have SC Senate (Andrews 53%) favored D; MS Colom 46.6%.

silver.name: Silver Bulletin (FLIPR)
silver.notes: FLIPR model covering Senate, House and governors; final update early Nov 3, 2026 (frozen). Race-level probability tables are paywalled (live pages and Wayback both show only the free preview; Wayback also rate-limited us). Race-level numeric probabilities therefore NOT recorded. Per-race entries give (a) which side FLIPR favored, read from Silver's own Nov 5 post 'Models led prediction markets' (free) which plots FLIPR vs Polymarket for every Senate and governor race as of Nov 3 (charts have no data labels, so only the side of 50% and a coarse 10-pt band are recorded), (b) Silver Bulletin category rating per the Wikipedia predictions table (col dated Nov 3; secondary), and (c) Silver Bulletin polling average quoted by Newsweek Nov 3 (a poll average, NOT the model's projected margin). Earlier datapoints: SC Andrews 27% (~Oct 25) and 31% (~Oct 28) per Silver's own 'Some thoughts on South Carolina' post; Oct 5 governor probabilities via InteractivePolls (NV Ford 47, TX Hinojosa 31, VT Janoo 24) — not final.

split_ticket.name: Split Ticket (published at The Argument)
split_ticket.notes: Senate + House model only; NO governor forecast found (Argument model post has only Senate/House charts; no governor model on split-ticket.org or in Argument archive search; Wikipedia gov table lists no ST column). Final values are the last published Datawrapper versions (older version URLs redirect to these; no later version exists). Senate charts publishedAt 2026-11-02 00:25-04:31Z; House model table u9EZf v36 published 2026-11-03T04:07Z; House prob/seat charts last published 2026-10-31T17:19Z. All charts show lastModifiedAt 2026-11-03T04:06-04:08Z without a newer published version. Wayback (web.archive.org) refused connections from this environment, so the 20261103212756 snapshot could not be cross-checked. p_dem for NE/MT/ID/SD is the independent candidate's probability. Margin sign: positive = Dem/Ind lead. Win probs published as integers.

racetothewh.name: Race to the WH (Logan Phillips)
racetothewh.notes: Covers Senate, Governor and House. Data read from the Google-Sheets-backed Infogram live-data feeds fetched 2026-11-11; the feeds were not updated after the election: Senate stamped 'Nov 3, 12:12 AM ET', Governor 'Nov 3, 12:01 AM ET', House 'Nov 3, 2:36 PM ET' (Election Day, before polls closed). The national trend sheets' last point is 'Nov 3' and matches (Senate 81.2%, House 96.2%). Newsweek (Nov 2) quoted 79.4% / 53 seats for the Senate, apparently an earlier run (trend shows 77.5% on Oct 30, 81.2% on Nov 3); the Nov 3 value is used here. Win probabilities to 0.1%. p_dem for MT/NE/ID/SD is the independent. Projected seats are means; the Senate median was computed from the published seat distribution. Governor: only a mean count of D-held governorships (26.8 of 50) is published, no median. Wayback was unreachable from this environment for a cross-check. The only risk: a live sheet could in principle be edited after Nov 3, but every stamp and trend endpoint reads Nov 3.
